comments.content: `alloc` is registered as a jemalloc extent hook, which is invoked from jemalloc's C code. Throwing a C++ exception (`std::runtime_error`) across this C boundary on `madvise` failure is undefined behavior and can corrupt the allocator state / crash. On failure you should not throw here — instead log the error (or increment a metric) and still return `result`, since the extent was allocated successfully and only the MADV_DONTDUMP hint failed.

`dallocx(p, flags)` has undefined behavior if `p` is null. `AwsNodumpMemoryManager::FreeMemory` forwards directly here and the AWS SDK does not always guarantee a non-null pointer. Consider guarding with `if (p) dallocx(...)`.

`USE_AWS_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT` is defined here but is not referenced anywhere in this PR (the actual guards use `USE_AWS_S3` and `USE_JEMALLOC`). Either wire it into the relevant `#if` checks (e.g. in Client.cpp / AwsNodumpMemoryManager) or drop it to avoid dead configuration.

`toNoDumpString` takes the std::string by value and copies it, but the source key still resides in normal (dumpable) heap memory (e.g. the `config.getString(...)` result). The sensitive bytes therefore live in a core-dumpable buffer before/after this copy, weakening the guarantee. Consider passing by const-ref plus explicitly scrubbing the temporary, or documenting this limitation.
